said by tmesis for συγγηράναι [to grow old together]. In M νῦν δὲ [now but], which Auratus corrected. But γηράναι (γηρᾶναι M) [to grow old] is an aorist infinitive as if from γήρημι [I grow old], which the scholiast noted with the words ἀπὸ τοῦ γήρημι [from γήρημι]. The correct accent is γηράναι [to grow old], not γηρᾶναι [to grow old], about which I spoke in Thes. vol. 2 p. 609.

May only Might and Justice, with the third, greatest of all, Zeus, be with you (thus Stanleius for μοι [me]).
And be with us against our enemies.

to which Danaus replies at 216 συγγνοῖτο δῆτα καὶ παρασταίη πρόφρων [may he indeed pardon and stand by willingly], where the use of the middle form is to be noted. Moreover, in the earlier passage M has εὐγνώη [may he be well-disposed] (which Robertellus had changed to συγγνώη [may he pardon], Lobeckius restored the correct form συγγνοίη [may he pardon] in his note on Phryn. p. 347), in the latter σύγνοιτο [may he pardon], with ν added above y and in the margin by a corrector συγγένοιτο [may he be with]. Victorius rightly reads σύγγνοῖτο [may he pardon].
CHORUS: Knowing this fate, Apollo would pardon mortals,
may he indeed pardon and stand by willingly
by a corrector may he be with
it is akin to mortals to kick the fallen man all the more
to drag down together with others
to drag down together with others
But this prophet, a prudent, just, good, pious man, mixed with the impious, will be dragged down together.
to establish together, to set up together with someone
to establish together, to set up together with someone
this friend of Zeus, who helped establish the tyranny
to be covered, to be concealed
to be covered, to be concealed
(the word) is to be concealed as much as possible
and the savour and the covered limbs
you who suffer with the misfortunes of this man
which the scholiast explains as συνάρασθαι πρὸς τὴν ὁδόν [to join in the journey].
for now deceitful Persuasion is at its peak to go down together
Thus Zeus and Fate went down together.
